* The terminal a frame is drawn on travels with the frame (rich-animation-27tq.lfw)

Every colour effect was handed the terminal when it was built, so two effects
in one frame could name different terminals, and a user container's caller had
to carry it down to the leaves. It is now `RenderOptions.terminal`, beside
`colorSystem`: a program names it once on its Console, App or renderToString,
and `Recolored.moved` is the one read of it. ProgressBar reads it too, where it
had hard-coded the depth's assumed terminal.

`theme` comes off `EffectedOptions`, `throughColors` and `Between`.
`Drawn.theme` becomes `Drawn.terminal`, since `RenderOptions.theme` already
means the style names. Each is a compile error for a caller, not a silent
change. `drawnOf` keeps its argument: it measures segments the caller holds and
builds no effect.

* Review: a test's terminal is named, and drawnOf reads absent as a frame does (rich-animation-27tq.lfw)

effect-seams had lost its terminals: every row drew on the assumed one, so a
seam resolved apart from its neighbours passed. With `terminal: theme` back,
breaking only `_rejoined` fails 84 of its rows; without it, none.

`drawnOf` takes `options.terminal` as it stands, since `resolveTerminal` is not
public and a renderable could not say what absent means. The pulse builds from
the `Drawn` it is handed, and the private recolouring helpers take that `Drawn`
for the depth and terminal it already carries. "The one read" was false, since
the bar must read the terminal before `Effected` runs to name its back.

The gruvbox tour section and the steppedInk live fence name their terminals
again, and docs/effects.md stops describing a `theme` option.

* Review: every test that names a terminal draws on it, and every road is tried (rich-animation-27tq.lfw)

next-change and on-beat had lost Mocha; on-beat drew on the assumed terminal and
measured on Mocha. change.test compared a ground it no longer drew on. The
terminal test now covers Live and WidgetApp beside App, and stops what it runs.

docs/protocol.md names `terminal` beside `colorSystem`, and the two leftover
mentions of a theme an effect reads now say terminal.
